blocks.content: Quiz: What is stored in ref.current after you attach a ref to a JSX element?
Tap an option below to answer:
A copy of the JSX element
ref.current is not a React element. It's the underlying browser DOM node.
ref.current is not a React element. It's the underlying browser DOM node.
The component's state at the time of render
Refs and state are completely separate. A ref holds a DOM reference, not state.
Refs and state are completely separate. A ref holds a DOM reference, not state.
The actual DOM node — the browser element React rendered
After React renders the element, ref.current points to the real DOM node, not a React element.
After React renders the element, ref.current points to the real DOM node, not a React element.
The function that last updated the element
Refs don't track what caused an update. They hold a reference to the DOM node itself.
Refs don't track what caused an update. They hold a reference to the DOM node itself.
